findings.reason: _is_error_focused_query does a plain substring check for "event.type:error", so `!event.type:error` and OR queries also match, and with the discover dataset their transaction counts get rewritten to sum(sample_weight) and come out wrong.

I confirmed that _get_event_stats passes the closure's `dataset` (a metrics dataset whenever the dashboard-split path at line 344 runs) and request.GET's query instead of scoped_dataset/split_query, so error-split widgets that query discover are never upsampled.

resolve_function stores the full function string ("upsampled_count() as count") as FunctionDetails.field, and process_results renames output columns to that string when transform_alias_to_input_format is set, while the serializer looks up the untransformed "count()", so the mismatch looks real; the finding is phrased as a confirm-request, which caps it.
The diff adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink and the repo has no .gitmodules, so it is clearly an accidental commit; it is cleanup that should be removed but has no runtime impact.
It is true that the cache get/set runs before the cheap dataset check on every request and only saves an options lookup; this is a marginal performance/staleness improvement.
invalidate_upsampling_cache has no callers, and the docstring's claim of a fresh read every time contradicts the 60s cache around it; this is a dead-code and docs inconsistency.
sum() does skip NULL sample_weight, so events stored without a weight would drop out of the count, but this depends on unverified ingestion behaviour and the finding is phrased as a question.
CLAUDE.md item 7 does say to use the self.create_* helpers, and the test calls Organization.objects.create directly; this is a trivial style issue.
